[doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
When projected capacity for the rest of the program (average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left) is larger than the untouched doors left in our turf, we will run out of first-pass turf. In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

[doc:counting-doors#doors]
A door is one address unit (a house, or one apartment unit) knocked on one day. Our dashboard counts each door once per day no matter how many times it was knocked that day. Doors knocked on different days count again on each day, so a second pass on a not-home door adds a door on the day of the second pass.

[doc:counting-doors#attempts]
An attempt is every knock record the canvassing app submits. If a canvasser knocks a not-home door at 11:00 and comes back at 14:00, that is two attempts and one door. Attempts are always equal to or higher than doors.

[doc:qc-rules#apartments-and-units]
Every apartment unit is its own door and must be knocked on its own. If a building is locked and the canvasser cannot get in, record the building once as "inaccessible" on its first unit and move on; do not mark each unit. A canvasser who marks a whole building from the lobby is householding.

args.query: not home doors count definition last knock

result:
[doc:counting-doors#doors]
A door is one address unit (a house, or one apartment unit) knocked on one day. Our dashboard counts each door once per day no matter how many times it was knocked that day. Doors knocked on different days count again on each day, so a second pass on a not-home door adds a door on the day of the second pass.

[doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

[doc:counting-doors#attempts]
An attempt is every knock record the canvassing app submits. If a canvasser knocks a not-home door at 11:00 and comes back at 14:00, that is two attempts and one door. Attempts are always equal to or higher than doors.

[doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]
The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.

args.query: householding flash knocking flags in a week escalate to field director

result:
[doc:qc-rules#what-happens-after-a-flag]
Every open flag needs a conversation between the field lead and the canvasser before the canvasser's next shift, using the timestamped evidence on the flag. After the conversation the flag is marked reviewed. Two or more householding or flash knocking flags in one week for the same canvasser go to the field director.

[doc:qc-rules#flash-knocking]
Flash knocking is recording doors faster than a person can walk to them and knock. A shift is flagged when 10 or more consecutive knocks are recorded less than 30 seconds apart. Confirmed flash knocking is rolled back: the knocks in the window no longer count as doors or contacts. A whole shift recorded this way is rolled back in full.

[doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

[doc:qc-rules#gaps]
A gap flag is raised when a canvasser is clocked in but records no knocks for 60 minutes or more. Gaps can be legitimate (a long conversation, a turf change, a break that was not clocked out), so the canvasser explains it before any pay adjustment.

[doc:registration-drive#qc-calls]
A sample of valid cards gets a QC call a day or two after collection. Outcomes are confirmed (the registrant confirms they filled out the card), unreachable (no answer after two tries) and wrong_info (the person says the details are wrong or they did not register). Wrong information above 10 percent of calls for a canvasser is escalated.

[doc:qc-rules#qc-rate]
The QC rate is flags per 100 GOTV shifts for an office in a week. Week over week trends use this rate, not raw flag counts, because the number of shifts grows during the program.

[doc:counting-doors#rollbacks]
When QC confirms flash knocking, the knocks in the flagged window are rolled back: they stay in the data with rolled_back = true but are removed from doors and contacts. Rollbacks happen after the day's client report has been pulled, so they never change a report that was already sent.

[doc:counting-doors#why-the-client-s-numbers-differ-from-ours]
The client daily report counts attempts, pulled at the end of each day before any QC rollback. Our dashboard counts doors with rollbacks removed. The gap on any day is the repeat attempts at the same door plus any attempts that were later rolled back. A normal day shows a gap of a few percent from repeat attempts. A larger gap almost always means a rollback.

[doc:registration-drive#cards-per-hour]
Cards per hour is valid cards divided by paid registration hours. Current pace uses the last 7 days. The cards per hour needed from here is the cards still needed (goal minus valid cards) divided by the hours we expect to work before the deadline: average daily registration hours of the last 7 days times days left. An office is under the needed rate when its last 7 days rate is below the program-wide rate needed.

[doc:client-reporting#weekly-report-format]
Every Monday we send the client one table for the week that ended Sunday, one row per office plus a total: doors, contacts, registration cards, and paid hours. Doors and contacts use our dashboard definitions (doors once per day, rollbacks removed). Cards are valid registration cards, duplicates removed. Hours are paid hours for GOTV and registration shifts together; shifts still missing a clock out are left out and noted.

[doc:registration-drive#valid-cards-and-duplicates]
A card is one completed registration form. A duplicate is a second card for a registrant who already has a card in the drive; duplicates share a duplicate group id with the first card and are marked is_duplicate. Only valid cards (duplicates removed) count toward goal and cards per hour. A canvasser with a duplicate rate above 10 percent gets a retraining conversation.

[doc:payroll-rules#cost-per-door]
Cost per door is GOTV wages (paid hours times the hourly rate for the person's role) divided by doors for the same office and period. Overtime premiums are left out of this figure.

[doc:payroll-rules#pay-rates]
Canvassers are paid hourly by role: canvasser, field lead, registration canvasser and registration lead. Rates are in the pay rates table. Paid hours are clock in to clock out for each shift.

[doc:payroll-rules#overtime]
The overtime threshold is 40 paid hours in a payroll week, Monday through Sunday, counting every shift the person worked. Hours over 40 are paid at 1.5 times the hourly rate. Any shift that takes a person over 40 hours needs the field director's approval and stays pending until it is approved.

[doc:payroll-rules#cost-per-door]
Cost per door is GOTV wages (paid hours times the hourly rate for the person's role) divided by doors for the same office and period. Overtime premiums are left out of this figure.

[doc:payroll-rules#payroll-deadline]
Payroll for the week that ended Sunday runs Tuesday at noon. Every shift must be approved by Monday at 5 PM; pending and needs_fix shifts left after that roll to the next payroll.

[doc:payroll-rules#shifts-that-need-fixing]
A shift marked needs_fix cannot be paid until a field lead corrects it. Common reasons are a missing clock out (no paid hours yet) and a shift clocked under the wrong office. Fix the record, then mark it approved.

[doc:client-reporting#weekly-report-format]
Every Monday we send the client one table for the week that ended Sunday, one row per office plus a total: doors, contacts, registration cards, and paid hours. Doors and contacts use our dashboard definitions (doors once per day, rollbacks removed). Cards are valid registration cards, duplicates removed. Hours are paid hours for GOTV and registration shifts together; shifts still missing a clock out are left out and noted.

[doc:program-plan#shifts-needed]
Shifts per day needed is the doors still needed (total goal minus doors to date) divided by knocking days left, divided by the average doors per shift over the last 7 days. Extra shifts per day is that number minus the average shifts per day over the last 7 days. Field directors use this to set recruitment targets.

[doc:program-plan#overview]
Riverbend Votes is a paid GOTV door canvass run from three offices: Northside, Eastgate and Harbor. Knocking started Monday, September 21, 2026 and runs every day through Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Each office has its own turf (a list of precincts) and its own daily door goal that ramps up toward Election Day.

[doc:registration-drive#overview]
Riverbend Registers is a paid voter registration drive run from the same three offices, Northside, Eastgate and Harbor, with its own registration canvassers. Collection started September 21, 2026 and ends at the registration deadline, Friday, October 30, 2026. Each office has a card goal in the registration goals table.

[doc:program-plan#more-doors-or-a-second-pass]
When projected capacity for the rest of the program (average daily doors of the last 7 days times days left) is larger than the untouched doors left in our turf, we will run out of first-pass turf. In that case ask the client for more doors first; new turf contacts voters at the normal first-pass rate. A second pass on not-home doors is the fallback, because second passes contact voters at roughly half the first-pass rate. If untouched doors exceed capacity, keep working the turf we have.

[doc:program-plan#pace-and-projection]
Pace compares doors to date with the goal to date. The projection for Election Day assumes nothing changes: doors to date plus the average daily doors of the last 7 days times the knocking days left. An office "will miss goal" when its projection is below its total goal; the shortfall is the goal minus the projection.

[doc:payroll-rules#pay-rates]
Canvassers are paid hourly by role: canvasser, field lead, registration canvasser and registration lead. Rates are in the pay rates table. Paid hours are clock in to clock out for each shift.

[doc:client-reporting#daily-report]
The client receives a daily report per office pulled from the canvassing app at the end of each day. It lists attempts (labeled "doors" in the client's sheet) and contacts as submitted, before any QC rollback. We do not edit a daily report after it is sent.

[doc:program-plan#staff-definitions]
A regular canvasser has worked 5 or more days in the program. A one-day hire worked exactly one day. An active canvasser worked at least one shift in the last 7 days. These definitions apply to GOTV canvassers.

[doc:qc-rules#gaps]
A gap flag is raised when a canvasser is clocked in but records no knocks for 60 minutes or more. Gaps can be legitimate (a long conversation, a turf change, a break that was not clocked out), so the canvasser explains it before any pay adjustment.
